subject: Observability & evals: success criteria, tracing hooks, dashboards
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Lina Chen <lina.chen@oliveai.com>, OliveAI Team <team@oliveai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Observability & evals: success criteria, tracing hooks, dashboards

Thanks again for your time today — really appreciated the candid run-through of the pain you're seeing in production. Below is a concise recap from our side so we have alignment on scope and next steps.

Call recap (high level)
- Pain: unpredictable model regressions after model updates; long time to detect output quality drift.
- Pain: limited request-level observability — can’t trace a user request through the inference stack to correlate latency vs. prompt variants.
- Pain: lack of token-level cost visibility (hard to budget per feature).
- Current stack: OliveAI is running a mix of managed LLM endpoints + an in-house caching/proxy layer; traffic varies from bursty demo spikes to steady production streams.

Success criteria you confirmed
1) Regression detection: surface a >1% drop in key evaluation metrics within 24 hours of rollout.
2) Latency: p95 inference latency <300ms for 512-token median workload.
3) Cost visibility: token-level breakdown per route and per-customer segment.
4) Safe rollouts: canary with automatic rollback on quality regressions.

Observability & evals scope we discussed
- Dashboards: token cost, per-model latency histograms, failure rates by route, eval metric trendlines (precision/recall/avg logprob).
- Tracing: want per-request traces (OpenTelemetry preferred), ability to join traces with your upstream request IDs.
- Golden prompts: you’ll provide a 50–100 prompt seed set (golden prompts) that we’ll run during evals and then include in continuous regression monitoring.
- Regression alerts: configurable thresholds and Slack/email alerting; want daily digest + immediate page for major regressions.

Immediate next steps (our ask of OliveAI)
1) Share the golden prompt seed set and a small sample (100–500) of recent production prompts (anonymized).
2) Confirm procurement contact for a short POC contract (we can handle NDAs + data handling in parallel).
3) Provide a tech contact for tracing hook integration (we’ll send a small OpenTelemetry snippet).

Deliverables from Redwood
- A 2-week eval plan and sandbox link to run the golden prompts against a candidate model.
- A lightweight tracing snippet + integration guide for adding request IDs to Redwood traces.
- A dashboard wireframe and a proposal with pricing for a 30-day POC.

Attachments: oliveai_poc_requirements.xlsx (POC checklist we discussed)

Tentative timeline
- Week 1: exchange artifacts (prompts, sample traffic, procurement questionnaire)
- Week 2: deploy eval sandbox, run golden prompts, demo initial dashboard
- Week 3: iterate on alerts and rollout guardrails; present final POC report

If that aligns, I’ll send the eval plan + sandbox invite today and loop Marissa for the demo scheduling. Thanks again — excited to move forward.

—
Logan Wright
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Lina Chen <lina.chen@oliveai.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: OliveAI Procurement <procurement@oliveai.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability & evals: success criteria, tracing hooks, dashboards

Thanks Logan — this matches our notes. Appreciate the clear success criteria. A couple quick clarifications: 

- Golden prompts: we'll start with ~60 prompts that capture our top 10 user intents. We can export anonymized examples from production — will scrub PII.
- Latency target: 300ms p95 is realistic for our non-augmented routes; for longer context LLMs we may accept a slightly higher p95 during the POC, but we want to track it precisely.

Procurement / legal next steps
- Looping in procurement to start the usual POC paperwork; attached is our procurement_questionnaire.pdf — please have legal/finance fill the applicable fields.

Tech contact
- I'll connect you to our infra lead, Priya Rao (priya.rao@oliveai.com), for tracing hooks and sample traffic.

Thanks — Lina

--
Lina Chen
Head of Product, OliveAI
lina.chen@oliveai.com | +1 (646) 222-9876

Attachment: procurement_questionnaire.pdf

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Lina Chen <lina.chen@oliveai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability & evals: success criteria, tracing hooks, dashboards

Perfect — thanks Lina. Quick updates based on your email: 

1) We’ll take the 60 golden prompts as our initial seed and request the additional 100 anonymized sample prompts during week 1.
2) I’ve uploaded a 2-week eval plan and sandbox invite here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Aq2b-example-eval-plan — Marissa will run the initial demo session once we get access to sample traffic.
3) Procurement: our finance/legal will complete the procurement_questionnaire and return it to procurement@oliveai.com by Wednesday.

Marissa — can you lead the demo and confirm availability next Wednesday (Aug 25) or Thursday (Aug 26) morning PT?

Sergio — on tracing: Lina suggested Priya Rao as tech contact. We’ll send the lightweight OTel snippet; Sergio, can your team validate the header propagation requirements below?

Technical ask summary (we discussed on the call)\- Add request-id to incoming user requests (header x-olive-request-id or x-request-id)\- Propagate that id into Redwood traces and model engine spans\- One span per inference call; include model_id, route, input_length tokens, output_length tokens as span attributes\- Sampling: start with 10% sampled traces for the POC; increase to 100% for failing requests or flagged prompts

I’ll start the procurement thread and attach the POC checklist (oliveai_poc_requirements.xlsx).

Thanks — Logan

—
Logan Wright
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Lina Chen <lina.chen@oliveai.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability & evals: success criteria, tracing hooks, dashboards

Adding a few implementation-level notes for Priya / OliveAI infra to speed the integration: 

1) OTEL snippet: we’ll send a Node/Python snippet that attaches x-olive-request-id and maps it to traceparent. Minimal example will be included in tracing_hook_snippet.txt.
2) Headers & attributes:
   - model_id (string)
   - route (string)
   - input_tokens (int)
   - output_tokens (int)
   - cache_hit (bool)

3) Sampling policy suggestion for the POC:
   - baseline: 10% random sample
   - anomalies: sample 100% of requests with error/latency > 2x p95
   - golden prompts: always sample golden prompts during evaluation runs

4) Data retention & privacy:
   - For the POC we recommend 30-day retention on payloads, with automatic token scrubbing of PII fields supplied in the prompt templates.
   - If OliveAI requires longer retention for auditing, we’ll surface options and cost impact.

5) Regression monitoring: we’ll wire a daily job that runs golden prompts and posts a delta report (accuracy / avg logprob / response length) to the dashboard. Threshold-based alerts can page on >1% metric drop.

I attached a short tracing_hook_snippet.txt that your infra team can drop into the request path — Priya, happy to jump on a 30-minute pairing session to validate.

—
Sergio Alvarez
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0199

Attachment: tracing_hook_snippet.txt
